privacy.heading: Who we are
paragraphs: LegalHub is a legal practice-management app with a Legal Library module. The app is offered for demonstration; it is operated by the owner identified in the in-app contact constant. This draft was generated from a code review and requires review by qualified counsel before production use.

privacy.heading: What we collect
paragraphs: Account email and display name; your role and organization memberships; matters, documents and message metadata; invoices and notifications; Legal Library bookmarks, highlights and reading history; AI research run metadata and video session metadata. The demo build uses synthetic records and no real client data.

privacy.heading: How it is processed
paragraphs: Data is stored in Supabase Postgres with row-level security. Practice data is organization-scoped; Legal Library reference content is global; bookmarks, highlights and history are visible only to you. Mutations go through server-side functions that derive your identity from the session.

privacy.heading: Storage and files
paragraphs: Files are kept in a private storage bucket at 25 MiB maximum per file with a restricted file-type allowlist. Access to a file requires active membership in its organization and assignment to its matter.

privacy.heading: What we do not collect
paragraphs: The app contains no analytics SDK, no advertising and no third-party crash-reporting SDK. Errors are reported through a redacting console reporter. Payment collection, AI research and video calls are provider-gated and disabled unless explicitly configured.

privacy.heading: Your controls
paragraphs: You can edit your display name and change your password in Account settings. You can delete your account from the same screen after reading exactly what is removed. You can clear your reading history in the Library Saved screen.

privacy.heading: Deletion and contact
paragraphs: Account deletion removes your sign-in, profile, memberships, Legal Library rows and your file records with their metadata. Stored file bytes on hosted deployments are removed by the operator's storage cleanup, not by the in-app step. It does not remove records owned by other people or provider-side records. Redacted audit entries are retained with the actor reference cleared. For questions, use the contact address in the in-app legal notice. A service-role cleanup function is provided in code but is not deployed yet; deletion stays partial until the operator deploys it and verifies that the bytes are gone.

terms.heading: Informational only
paragraphs: LegalHub provides informational software. Nothing in the app, including AI-generated research and sample Legal Library content, is legal advice or a substitute for a qualified lawyer.

terms.heading: No attorney-client relationship
paragraphs: Using the app does not create an attorney-client relationship. The attorney directory contains professional profile data only; no credential verification is performed.

terms.heading: Sample content
paragraphs: The bundled Legal Library corpus is artificial demonstration data. Every sample row is labelled in the interface. Real legal text must be imported from an authoritative source by the operator and reviewed before reliance.

terms.heading: Your responsibilities
paragraphs: Use the app lawfully, do not upload content you are not entitled to store, and do not attempt to access data belonging to another organization or another user.

terms.heading: Accounts and termination
paragraphs: You are responsible for keeping your credentials secure. You may delete your account in Account settings; some redacted audit records are retained after deletion. The operator may restrict access where required to protect other users or the service.

terms.heading: Warranties and liability
paragraphs: The software is provided as-is without warranties. To the extent permitted by law, the operator is not liable for indirect or consequential loss arising from its use. Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited.

terms.heading: Governing law
paragraphs: The governing law and venue must be filled in by the operator before production use. No jurisdiction is asserted by this draft.
